assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting circuits into controllable artificial atoms strongly coupled to single microwave photons, giving dispersive readout, coupling buses and the architecture of today's superconducting processors. It is conceptually original (the Blais et al. 2004 proposal), experimentally decisive (Wallraff et al. 2004) and has generated a whole field, including waveguide QED and microwave quantum optics. Seen from my own subfield I judge this the clearest foundational step beyond the macroscopic quantum phenomena recognised in 2025.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff, Schuster, Blais, Frunzio, Huang, Schoelkopf and others) support a Blais / Wallraff / Schoelkopf configuration. Girvin and Huang are not in the supplied credited names and could be argued for; I cannot add them. I have a field-adjacent interest and work in this area, so I note that my view of the credit split is not fully detached.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than twenty years of independent confirmation across many laboratories and platforms, stable interpretation, and direct technological uptake in quantum processors. Recognition is timely, with the 2025 prize recently awarded for the underlying circuit physics rather than for this step.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should combine the proposal and the first experiment or give priority to one
Overlap with the 2025 award for circuit quantum physics could be seen as too close by some members
Omitted contributors (for example Girvin, Huang, Devoret-related work) cannot be included from this credit list

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled trapped ions and neutral atoms as quantum processors and simulators: the Cirac-Zoller gate proposal, ion-trap implementations of entangling gates, algorithms and error-correction demonstrations, and analogue simulation with cold atoms. This is a broad, high-impact pillar of quantum information science with clear conceptual and experimental content.
assessment.attribution: Theory and experiment are naturally paired: Cirac and Zoller for the proposals and Blatt for the leading ion-trap realisations. Bloch is credited mainly for optical-lattice simulation and is left off to keep a three-person group, which makes a choice that others could contest. Wineland's ion-control work was already recognised in 2012, so the new increment must be clear.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by many groups for ions and neutral atoms. Digital ion-trap computing is advancing but still scaling, so the prize would honour methods more than a finished technology.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for controlling single quantum systems
Compound candidate whose ion and neutral-atom parts might merit different recognition
Exclusion of Bloch is a judgement about which strand to emphasise

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson at the LHC in 2012 confirmed the mechanism recognised in 2013 and is among the most consequential experimental results in particle physics. It required the design of two very different general-purpose detectors and an enormous collaborative effort.
assessment.attribution: Credit rests with the founding and leading figures of ATLAS and CMS rather than single discoverers. Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee conceived and led the experiments from the early proposals; Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of the announcement and has a strong claim. A three-person limit means a hard choice, and an institutional alternative is not available under the prize rules as I read them.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: observed independently by two experiments, with couplings measured at the LHC in the following decade. Recognition is long overdue in the sense that the theory prize was given in 2013.
uncertainties: Allocation among many leaders of two large collaborations is unavoidably arbitrary
Whether the committee wants to honour detector conception or the discovery announcement

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator by Kane and Mele, followed by its observation in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group, opened a major area of topological condensed matter physics with concrete materials, protected edge transport and links to quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: The Kane-Mele proposal and the Molenkamp experiment form a clear theory-plus-experiment configuration. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation and are not in the supplied credit list, so the allocation is incomplete and potentially contested. I judge this credit set better supported than the alternative topological-insulator candidate omitting Mele.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with many independent materials confirmations including three-dimensional topological insulators, though practical applications remain limited. It follows the 2016 topological-phases prize but concerns a distinct discovery.
uncertainties: Missing credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang)
Possible overlap with 2016 topological-phases prize in the committee's view
Overlap with the other topological-insulator candidate on the list

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter and a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators observed the correlated states. Cao and others contributed substantially to the experiments and are not in the credit list. The theory-experiment pairing is clean but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly developing and independently reproduced, but the origin of superconductivity and many correlated phases is still debated, so the interpretation is less stable. Timeliness is plausible though perhaps early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism for superconductivity is unresolved
Contribution of early-career experimentalists not in the credit list
May be premature relative to more settled candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error-correcting codes, including Shor's code, Steane's CSS codes and Kitaev's toric code, show that fault-tolerant quantum computing is possible in principle. Full-scale error correction is, in my view, the central requirement for useful quantum processors, so the conceptual importance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane established the first codes and Kitaev the topological surface-code route. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill and others are important but outside the credit list, so the configuration is partial. Shor's factoring algorithm is a separate achievement.
assessment.maturity: The theory is established, and recent experiments with superconducting and atomic qubits show below-threshold error suppression. But the practical impact is only now emerging, so a prize might be seen as slightly early; on the other hand it follows a natural arc after the 2025 award.
uncertainties: Experimental maturity is still recent and incomplete
Large community of contributors beyond the three credited
Whether the prize should reward theory ahead of full demonstrations

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Semiconductor spin qubits began with the Loss-DiVincenzo proposal and developed through gate-defined quantum dots in GaAs, Si and Ge, achieving single and two-qubit gates with high fidelity and compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo for the proposal and Vandersypen for leading experimental realisation is a sensible trio; Petta and others also made major experimental contributions and are credited but not selected. Priority among experimental groups is not fully clear.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is substantial and independent across groups, but scaling and competitiveness against other platforms are open, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Competition among qubit platforms makes long-term importance uncertain
Several experimental groups with comparable claims
Conceptual overlap with other quantum computing candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and later evidence for a blazar and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy at energies far beyond earlier detectors. It is a clear discovery with large instrument-building effort.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the conceptual and leadership figure; Karle and Spiering are key to the detector design and the analysis. Allocation within a very large collaboration is uncertain, and other leaders are not included in the supplied names. I am less qualified to judge the field details and rely on general knowledge.
assessment.maturity: Detection is statistically solid and consistent across analyses, while the source population is only partly understood. Recognition is timely given the progress in multi-messenger astronomy.
uncertainties: Origin of most of the neutrino flux remains unknown
Credit within the collaboration is difficult to allocate
My assessment of detector and analysis details is from general knowledge and not independently verified
